ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in triangle $ABC$, the angle bisectors of $\angle ABC$ and $\angle ACB$ intersect at point $P$. When $\angle A=60^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle BPC$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, since BP is the bisector of $\angle ABC$,\\
then $\angle PBC = \frac{1}{2}\angle ABC$. (Definition of an angle bisector)\\
Since CP is the bisector of $\angle ACB$,\\
then $\angle PCB = \frac{1}{2}\angle ACB$,\\
thus $\angle PBC + \angle PCB = \frac{1}{2}(\angle ACB + \angle ABC)$,\\
Since $\angle A = 60^\circ$,\\
then $\angle ACB + \angle ABC = 120^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle PBC + \angle PCB = \frac{1}{2}\left(\angle ACB + \angle ABC\right) = 60^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle BPC = 180^\circ - \angle PBC - \angle PCB = 180^\circ - (\angle PBC + \angle PCB) = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = \boxed{120^\circ}.$
